title: "The man whose name is the Branch" shall build the temple; a priest on his throne (Zech 6:9–15)
speaker: The LORD through Zechariah
description: Crowns made from the exiles' silver and gold are set on Joshua's head with the words: the man whose name is the Branch will branch out and build the LORD's temple, bear royal honour and rule on his throne; there will be a priest on his throne, and the counsel of peace between them both; those far off will come and build.
in_text_interpretation: The text names Joshua as the one crowned (MT) and the Branch as the builder; the two figures are not equated explicitly.

interpretations.label: Joshua's crowning typifies the Messiah, priest and king in one
proponents: C. F. Keil (1868): a typical act pointing to a man who would combine royalty and priesthood; Zerubbabel must not be interpolated
D. Guzik: the King-Priest Jesus (cf. Ps 110:4; Heb 7)
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: a royal crown ('aṭārâ) did not belong to the high priest, so the act signifies one who will "be a priest on his throne"; "speak to him" is singular (Keil). The Branch builds a temple that Guzik reads as God's people (Eph 2:19–22). Objection: Mitchell holds that the original text crowned Zerubbabel.

referents.symbol: The man whose name is the Branch

interpretations.label: Zechariah crowned (or meant to crown) Zerubbabel as the Branch; the text was altered to Joshua
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Zechariah and Haggai expected Zerubbabel to build the temple and fulfil the Messianic hopes (Zech 4:9; Hag 2:23); crowning Joshua would contradict them. A scribe adjusted the text when no Davidide ruled again and the high priest became head of the community. Historical evidence: Zerubbabel disappears from the record.
